title: fix(service-storage): the attach verb vouches for the one file it created, so members attach files again after #31031
body:
security#1 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibvynRbCtMndW8EHNGc

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：服务端附件动词 `attachFileAs` 以调用者身份插入 `sys_attachment` 时，为它在同一次调用里刚创建的那一个 `sys_file` 担保（`vouchForReference`，`@objectstack/core`）；写入时的引用校验对这一个对象/字段/id 不再问调用者的读权限，但仍探测它存在。其余一切仍按调用者判定。
- 为什么改：#31031 之后 `lookup` 引用只能指向调用者读得到的记录，而成员一般读不到 `sys_file`，于是成员经 `attachFileAs` 上传附件、以及打印存档到附件（`printRecordToFile`）一律失败（500，"File: no sys_file record has id …"）。本 PR 恢复这两条路径，#31031 的通用规则不变。
- 风险与回滚：风险低。担保是 symbol 键的上下文属性，请求体、查询、存储行、流程定义都拼不出来；只对该次插入、该字段、该 id 生效。任何数据门（REST、MCP、流程、导入）送来的 `sys_file` id 照旧按调用者读权限判。回滚即撤本 PR，成员附件会重新失败。
- 先看：`packages/objectql/src/engine-referential-integrity.ts` 中 `callerReads` 一行；`packages/services/service-storage/src/file-attachment-service.ts` 步骤 ⑤ 的插入；`packages/core/src/security/vouched-reference.ts`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-storage exec vitest run src/file-attachment-service.test.ts`，预期 32/32 绿，其中成员上传附件一组 7 条。
- 需要你做的：请决定下方 Acceptance notes 第一条（浏览器附件面板的两步上传同样被 #31031 拦下）走哪条路。

## What changes

Restores member attachments after #31031. That PR made a non-system write's `lookup` / `master_detail` / `user` reference resolve only through the caller's own read door, and that rule stands. The server-side attach verb writes its `sys_attachment` row as the caller, and that row's `file_id` names the `sys_file` the same call has just created for the caller. A member who may attach files need not read `sys_file`. So the reference check refused the verb's own row, and both `attachFileAs` and print-to-attachment failed for every such member.

**The rule.** A service verb that has created a record in the same call may vouch, on its own write, for the one reference to that record. For exactly that object, field and id, the write-time reference check does not ask the caller's read door, and it still runs the elevated, tenant-kept existence probe. Nothing else on the write is admitted by it.

- `packages/core/src/security/vouched-reference.ts` adds `vouchForReference` / `isVouchedReference` and the `VOUCHED_REFERENCES` key. It is the same shape as the flow-write mark (`FLOW_WRITE_REFERENCE_CHECK`): a `Symbol.for` key that sits in no schema, does not survive `ExecutionContextSchema.parse`, and cannot be spelled by any request body, query string, stored row or flow definition.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-referential-integrity.ts`: `assertReferencesResolve` asks the caller's read door for every `lookup` / `user` / `master_detail` value except a vouched one, which goes to the existence probe alone.
- `packages/services/service-storage/src/file-attachment-service.ts`: the caller-scoped `sys_attachment` insert vouches for `sys_attachment.file_id` = the file id created in step ③. The system path (`attachFile`) carries no mark, because system writes are already exempt.

**Why this seam.** I looked at three other shapes and did not use them:

- An `ExecutionContext` key or an engine option. Either would add to the spec's Zod contract.
- A system-elevated insert of the link. That drops the caller's RLS, FLS, the `uploaded_by` stamp, the parent-edit attach rule and the object permission on `sys_attachment`.
- Admitting a `sys_file` the caller uploaded (`owner_id`) inside the generic rule. That special-cases one object in the generic engine, and it widens every data door.

The mark keeps the insert as the caller's own write. Every other gate still judges the caller: object permission to create an attachment, parent edit (`installAttachmentAccessHooks`), `enable.files`, the file-reference gate (`installAttachmentFileReferenceGate`, the download door's verdict on the file), RLS, FLS, and the owner and audit stamps. The caller's other references, the parent included, are judged as before. No read is widened.

## Tests

Final-head local runs are in the Verification section below.

- `packages/services/service-storage/src/file-attachment-service.test.ts` gets a new top-level describe. It runs a real ObjectQL over sqlite with an engine middleware standing in for the object-permission layer: a non-system read of `sys_file` is refused `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403.
  - Pins: a member attaches through `attachFileAs`. The attachment is `uploaded_by` the member and the file is owned by them. The print sequence (`assertMayAttach`, then `attachFileAs`) also attaches as the member.
  - Controls: `assertMayAttach` still refuses a member the attach rule refuses. A parent the member cannot read is refused `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` / 404. The member's own data-engine insert of `sys_attachment` naming a file they cannot read is refused `VALIDATION_FAILED` / `reference_not_found`, and so is the same insert naming the very file the verb attached.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-unreadable-reference-target.test.ts` gets a new top-level describe.
  - The vouched value lands and only the elevated probe runs.
  - A vouched id that names no row is still refused.
  - Another unreadable id in the same field, the same id in another field, and the same id on another object are each refused.
  - A multi-valued field admits only the vouched member.
  - A context without the mark is refused, and so is one carrying the symbol's description as a plain string key.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/print-service-archive.dogfood.test.ts` runs on a real showcase boot.
  - A member holding the contributor set and a `sys_attachment` read/create grant, and nothing on `sys_file`, prints their own invoice to its attachments. The attachment names them, and `sys_file` stays unreadable to them afterwards.
  - Control: the same member's own `sys_attachment` insert naming a file they own and cannot read is refused `reference_not_found`.

**Ablations.** Each was run on a committed fix, with the restore proved by blob hash against HEAD.

- Storage side, with the vouch removed from the insert. The suite reads storage source directly, so no build was needed. The two member-attach pins and the same-file pin go red (3 failed, 29 passed). The four controls stay green.
- Engine side, with `isVouchedReference` removed from `callerReads`. objectql was rebuilt and `ablation-dist-preflight` confirmed the marker absent from all 14 built files.
  - objectql pins: 4 failed, 117 passed. The 4 red are the admitting pins; the nowhere, other-id, other-object and unmarked controls stay green.
  - storage pins: 3 failed, 29 passed.
  - print dogfood: the member print is red; 10 passed, the control included.
  - The restore leg was rebuilt and the preflight found the marker present in 4 built files.
- #31009's `showcase-mcp-record-files.dogfood.test.ts` lives only on that PR's branch. It was run in a scratch tree: this branch merged with `origin/claude/project-thread-s2vcdk` (head `c2a3229be1`) and not pushed. Result: 13 of 13 pass. With the engine-side ablation in that same tree, exactly the three attachment cases go red (3 failed, 10 passed), matching the 3-of-13 regression measured after `eb96480dd6`.

## Acceptance notes

1. **The browser attachments panel's two-step flow is refused the same way, and this PR does not change that.**
   - What fails: the panel uploads through the presigned door, then posts `POST /data/sys_attachment` with the returned `file_id` through the generic data door. That post answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, `file_id` `reference_not_found`, for a member who holds the `sys_attachment` create grant and nothing on `sys_file`.
   - Measured on this branch: a showcase boot with a member holding `showcase_contributor` plus a `sys_attachment` read/create grant. Presign 200, PUT 200, complete 200, attach 400. The probe file was not committed.
   - Why main stays green: `attachments-permission-matrix.dogfood.test.ts` runs on a fixture baseline that grants `'*'` read, `sys_file` included.
   - Why this PR leaves it: per the order, the generic rule is not loosened for any data door here. The decision is the seat's.
2. **Audit of other service-internal writes on `main`.** I scanned every insert/update in `packages/services/*/src` and `packages/plugins/*/src` whose options carry a context that is not obviously the system's, and found no second instance of this regression shape to fix.
   - `admin-user-endpoints.ts` (plugin-auth). The admin create door grants a permission set as the administrator: `sys_user_permission_set.user_id` names the `sys_user` the same call created. The door's platform-admin gate admits only callers who read every user. Measured: `create-user-permission-set.dogfood.test.ts` passes 4 of 4 on this branch, G1 (user and grant land together) included. Not changed.
   - `approval-service.ts` `mirrorStatusField`. It updates the record's status mirror with an attributed context. That writes a status value, not a reference. Not affected.
   - `service-automation` `crud-nodes.ts` (a flow writing as the user). This is a generic door by design, so the caller's references are judged. Not changed.
   - Everything else matched in those paths — device registry, connector connections/credentials, sharing, share links, approvals' rows, datasource secrets, settings audit, the storage metadata store and the backfills — writes as the system.
